prompt.content:
You are an expert at reading and analyzing futures contract specifications.
You will be provided with a contract specification document and asked specific questions about it.
Analyze the document carefully and provide precise answers.

Always include your final answer inside \boxed{}.

Example:
Q: What is the lot size for this contract?
A: Looking at the contract specification, the contract unit is stated as "$50 x S&P 500 Index". 
This means each contract represents $50 times the index value. Therefore, the lot size is \boxed{50}.

Contract: Sydney Future Exchange Mini SPI 200 Index Day Session Index Future
RIC Root: 2YMF
Exchange: XSFE
Specification URL: https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/participants/derivatives-market/equity-derivatives/asx-spi-200-and-mini-spi-200-brochure.pdf

Contract Specification:
"ASX Mini SPI 200 Index Futures (Sydney Futures Exchange Mini SPI 200 Index Day Session Index Future)

Contract Unit: A$5 multiplied by the S&P/ASX 200 Index

Underlying Index: S&P/ASX 200 Index

Contract Months: March, June, September, December (up to 6 quarter months may be listed)

Trading Hours (Sydney time):
- Day Session: 9:50am – 4:30pm
- After-hours session (if applicable, per ASX specifications at the time of the brochure)

Minimum Price Movement (Tick Size): 1 index point

Tick Value: A$5 per index point

Contract Value: Index level × A$5

Last Trading Day:
- The third Thursday of the contract month; if this is not a business day, the preceding business day

Final Settlement Price:
- Calculated as the Special Opening Quotation (SOQ) of the S&P/ASX 200 Index on the morning of the third Thursday of the contract month (or the preceding business day, as applicable), based on the first traded price of each constituent stock in the index

Settlement Type: Cash settled

Position Limits / Accountability:
- As determined and published by ASX 24 and may change from time to time

Contract Code (ASX 24):
- Mini SPI: AM (plus month and year codes per ASX convention)

Exchange / Market: ASX 24 (formerly Sydney Futures Exchange)

Trading and Clearing: Subject to the operating rules of ASX 24 and ASX Clear (Futures)

Margining: SPAN-based initial margin and daily variation margin, as calculated by ASX Clear (Futures)

Price Limits / Trading Halts:
- As per ASX 24 operating rules applicable to equity index futures

Last Trading Time:
- As specified by ASX 24 for the relevant contract month on the last trading day (aligned with the SOQ process on expiry day)

Note: This specification summary is taken from the ASX SPI 200 and Mini SPI 200 brochure, which is the official contract specification document for the Sydney Futures Exchange Mini SPI 200 Index Futures, including the day session contract."...

Contract Specification:
"JSE MARKET NOTICE 3418: INTRODUCTION OF EDM INDEX FUTURE ON THE FTSE/JSE AFRICAN BANKS INDEX (ALSI BANKS) (J835)

PRODUCT DESCRIPTION
The FTSE/JSE African Banks Index Future is a cash-settled futures contract based on the FTSE/JSE African Banks Index (J835). The contract allows market participants to gain exposure to, or hedge exposure to, the South African banking sector as represented in the FTSE/JSE equity index series.

UNDERLYING INDEX
Name: FTSE/JSE African Banks Index
JSE Code: J835
Index Provider: FTSE Russell in partnership with the JSE
Index Type: Equity sector index, consisting of African bank constituents listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

CONTRACT SPECIFICATION
Contract Type: Cash-settled index futures
Contract Size: ZAR 10 per index point (i.e. the Rand value of the contract is 10 times the level of the FTSE/JSE African Banks Index)
Currency: South African Rand (ZAR)
Price Quotation: Index points, quoted to two decimal places
Minimum Price Movement (Tick Size): 0.50 index points
Tick Value: ZAR 5.00 (0.50 index points × ZAR 10 per index point)
Contract Months: Standard quarterly cycle: March, June, September, December (or as otherwise specified by the JSE)
Listing Cycle: Up to four quarterly contracts may be listed at any point in time, or as otherwise determined by the Exchange
Last Trading Day: The third Thursday of the contract month, or the preceding business day if the third Thursday is not a business day, subject to JSE rules
Trading Hours: During normal JSE Equity Derivatives trading hours, as published by the JSE from time to time
Final Settlement Date: The first business day following the Last Trading Day, unless otherwise specified by the JSE

SETTLEMENT
Settlement Type: Cash settlement only
Final Settlement Price: The closing level of the FTSE/JSE African Banks Index on the Last Trading Day, as calculated and published by FTSE/JSE according to the index ground rules
Settlement Method: Cash difference...

On the business day following the last day of the contract’s observation period, or as otherwise determined and published by CFE.
